parsed.explanation: The dossier documents one of the strongest protective regimes in its region: constitutional protection of gender identity, hate-crime coverage, protected bathroom access, no-requirement legal recognition, conversion-therapy ban, and low regional victimisation rates. The negatives are largely resident-facing or institutional: prison practice lags the strong statute (with the 2018 damages award showing courts did provide relief — recourse worked), and a pending asylum-detention case raises genuine border-processing concerns for LGBTI arrivals, though undecided and unproven. Low police reporting of violence and workplace concealment are friction/ambivalence signals, not exposures. No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility bans, no police targeting, no organised violence documented. These are classic 0.85 conditions: strong acceptance with documented functioning remedies, limited friction and open questions.
